rationale: Different facts about GeoConfirmed (structure vs API/licensing).
El País's account of Ka-52s carrying Vikhr ATGMs in 2023 corroborates the Ka-52/Vikhr element of RUSI's threat assessment.
The general in-service description of Ukrainian fixed-wing ISR drones corroborates their use in early 2022; both draw on the same RUSI report.
Same source and figures; B adds the early-2025 95% point to the Lima share series.
Same assertion (Russian mesh-radio control of Gerans via COFDM modems and relays) from the same sources, extracted twice.
Both, from the same RUSI report, say 2022 drone use was commercial quadcopters and TB2s mainly for reconnaissance.
B details the Starlink-enabled Russian mid-range drone interdiction listed in A's era summary; both ISW-based.
Different facts about ISW ArcGIS items (creation date vs licence).
B's general description of Ka-52/Mi-35M with Vikhr/Ataka and lofted S-8 corroborates A, partly from the same RUSI source.
B's effects of the middle-strike campaign on the R-280 presuppose A's strikes there; shared sources.
A gives the date (March 2025) and element count (16) for the Kometa-M CRPA fitting B states generally.
Different assertions about Vezha/Avengers (detection function vs role in HQ streams).
Two independent outlets report Ukrainian counterattacks in Zaporizhzhia and eastern Dnipropetrovsk in early 2026.
Different facts about ISW map (update cadence vs infiltration layer creation date).
Same event (first Mirage 2000-5 arrival 6 Feb 2025) from the same source, extracted twice.
A's Avdiivka October 2023 battalion mechanized waves is an instance of the tactic in B; shared Frontelligence source.
RUSI's 19,547 Wagner dead at Bakhmut corroborates the Wagner attritional assault characterization; same RUSI source.
A identifies the developer; B's substantive assertion is a comparative judgment of the FPV model.
Different symbology facts (affiliation states vs echelon coding).
Different facts about Perpetua's map (features vs update/licence).
Same anecdote (a Mavic lasting six months near Donetsk in late 2022) from the same source, extracted twice.
B lists the current ISW legend; it does not show the December 2025 redefinition A asserts.
Different subjects (air force role vs AASM Hammer bomb).
A describes Obriy; B is a vendor list of simulators, only topically related.
A qualifies B's 2026 shift to jet Gerans by noting the Geran-3 was retired by August 2026 in favour of Geran-4/5.
RUSI's view that GMLRS/HIMARS devastated Russian C2 and logistics supports its view that their arrival ended the Donbas offensive; same claimant.
Use of FPV interceptors against Orlan/Zala supports the assessment that interceptors are thinning them out; same RUSI source.
HUR's count of 100+ KN-23/24 delivered corroborates that the KN-23/24 is North Korean-supplied and used by Russia.
148 KN-23/24 by early 2025 and "more than 100" by July 2026 are compatible as stated (lower bound); no clear relation.
B dates the addition of P1-SUN and Bullet to the UFDS military edition to August 2026.
A is a genre overview; B describes Obriy's features; no bearing.
A gives the exact date of the Lviv Oreshnik strike (8 Jan 2026) and adds May 2026 uses to B's summary.
Same ISW-sourced event (Starlink-equipped BM-35/Molniya-2 deep strikes on E-50 traffic); B frames it as the cutoff trigger.
Different subjects (peace-talk demands vs map legend).
Different facts about Pokrovsk infiltration (group size vs clothing/weather).
B's account of the unexploited Krynky lodgement corroborates A's Krynky as the last effort of the 2023 offensive; same RUSI source.
Oryx loss totals vs FPV hits on helicopters; different quantities.
Different facts about AMK Mapping (author vs legend).
A gives the exact date (21 Nov 2024) of the Dnipro Oreshnik strike that B summarizes.
Different symbology rules (hostile frame vs frame openness by domain).
